claims.quote: Monobactams are parenteral beta-lactam bactericidal antibiotics.

claims.text: Cross-allergy unlikely except with ceftazidime/cefiderocol (shared R1 side chain), so used for serious gram-negative infections in patients with serious beta-lactam allergy.
claims.quote: Aztreonam shares structural similarities with few other beta-lactams, making cross-hypersensitivity unlikely, except with ceftazidime and cefiderocol, which have similar R1 side chains. Thus, aztreonam is used mainly for severe aerobic gram-negative bacillary infections (including meningitis) in patients who have a serious beta-lactam allergy but who nevertheless require beta-lactam therapy.

claims.text: Nebulized antibiotics (eg, aztreonam, tobramycin) can cut sputum bacterial load and may cut exacerbations; evidence strongest in CF.
claims.quote: Nebulized antibiotics (eg, amikacin, aztreonam, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, tobramycin) can reduce sputum bacterial load, and may also reduce the frequency of exacerbations. The evidence supporting their use and benefit is strongest in patients with CF.

claims.text: Inhaled aztreonam (Cayston) is labeled for CF with P. aeruginosa.
claims.quote: CAYSTON is a monobactam antibacterial indicated to improve respiratory symptoms in cystic fibrosis (CF) patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa .

claims.text: Cayston: 75 mg nebulized 3 times a day for 28 days, then 28 days off.
claims.quote: one single-use vial (75 mg of aztreonam) reconstituted with 1 mL of sterile diluent administered 3 times a day for a 28-day course (followed by 28 days off CAYSTON therapy).

claims.text: Use a bronchodilator before each Cayston dose (short-acting 15 min–4 h before).
claims.quote: Patients should use a bronchodilator before administration of CAYSTON. Short-acting bronchodilators can be taken between 15 minutes and 4 hours prior to each dose of CAYSTON.
This preparation is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to aztreonam or any other component in the formulation.
